topic: A technically valid AI-made video physically rejected by a human-review gate
thesis: Technical QA and human acceptance are different release gates; the prototype expresses that difference as a miniature factory gag.

sources.notes: Exact local evidence: src/content/shorts/codex-research-first-en/codex-research-first-en.mp4, SHA-256 dffda12d3f90e2432c0d451cf2df0574bd2f571b0fcce54387c0b573bccc734c; its video-qa-report.md, SHA-256 768d3183bfa6a5d2ef05443a5b2f17a025f6051779aada85f86cd0ce3c53fba3; and Aaron's approved feedback in the current task. The factory action is a stylized reenactment, not footage of a literal review machine.

Official model-specific terms for Music v1 and v2. This internal prototype reuses the already selected music_v2 candidate; the applicable paid-plan rights must be reconfirmed before commercial publication.

facts.claim: The exact source video is 1920×1080 at 60 fps, its encoded mix measured about -16.2 LUFS, and a full decode test completed without errors.
facts.sensitivity: These checks describe delivery properties of one encoded file; they do not establish taste, authenticity, or viewer trust.

facts.claim: Aaron rejected the technically passing result because the music felt bad and the recreated demo visibly looked fake.
facts.sensitivity: The trapdoor and NOPE chute are a comic reenactment of the review outcome, not a literal recorded event or quotation.

facts.claim: The prototype reuses the selected Eleven Music music_v2 candidate B, song ID SnFlUsOCkAk3pCwoo2UG, through the retained Aaron Studio selection manifest.
facts.sensitivity: Internal prototype provenance is resolved; commercial publication still requires an active-plan rights recheck.
